lesson.grammar_point: present simple vs past simple in self-introduction

listenings.text: Right, so this is my third visit to Brazil this year, and I want to say one thing before we walk in. When I meet the local teams, I do not want the tour. I have seen the warehouse. What I want is ten minutes with the people who actually talk to the customers, because they know things the monthly report never says. And here is the honest part. My Portuguese is about four words long, and I know exactly how unfair that is. So when somebody speaks to me in English and stops in the middle of a sentence to look for a word, I am not listening to the English. I am listening to what they know. The people I remember from these visits are never the ones with perfect grammar. They are the ones who told me one thing about a customer that I could not have read anywhere.

People hear the word credit and they picture a bank, and then I explain what I actually do and they are always surprised. I work for a company that makes crop protection products, and I am responsible for the money side of the customer relationship. My customers are farms and the local dealers who sell to farms. A farm does not pay us every month like a phone bill. It pays after the harvest, so I am lending a whole season, not thirty days. I deal with growers who have bought from us for thirty years, and I deal with a dealer who opened last spring, and those two people need completely different conversations. I started here as an assistant in customer service in two thousand eleven. I moved into credit two years later, mostly because nobody else wanted the job. It turned out to be the most interesting desk in the building.
